reason: B ships a working, validated, accessible-by-default register (aria-live status, aria-invalid, range and empty handling, noscript fallback, static markup identical to the JS render) whose sample numbers are consistent across the hero, the timeline and the report, while A is clean, light and well-labelled but has nothing to operate and makes service claims the brief does not support. B's defects (ledger clipping at 1000-1180px, invisible skip link, 'XX' leak) are fixable CSS/one-line bugs; I would change my mind only if the mid-width clipping were treated as a release blocker and A's static proof were judged sufficient for this buyer.
